title: Bastian studies an amyloid biopsy
topic: A clinic studies amyloid deposits in a patient's biopsy: Bastian finds deposits of misfolded amyloid in dense plaques, the laboratory finds a tau protein, a scan reveals more plaques, the patient's daughter asks questions, Bastian explains the misfolding and gives the family a treatment plan

E.pred: gives the family the treatment plan

tail_E: The patient already forgets names and slowly loses his
target_note: 'memory' is the natural completion of 'the patient already forgets names and slowly loses his' - the amyloid plaques, the tau protein and the scan of the ten units set up the clinical picture, and the tail's 'forgets names' makes the lost faculty specific. The word occurs nowhere in the units or the tail (no 'memory', 'memories', 'memorises'), and neither does a German equivalent (Gedächtnis / Erinnerung / Erinnerungen); the units never name a symptom, so the tail alone fixes the slot. ' memory' is a single Pythia token (id 3541); Pythia-160m ranks it first after the all-English context (p ~ 0.51, next candidates 'attention' / 'ability' / 'mind' ~ 0.02)
author: LS-NEQ stimulus authoring (F20A, amyloid biopsy in the clinic, Bastian)
notes: Formulation A, domain protein_misfolding (DESIGN.md §4.8: the misfolding domain is the proposed counter-pole to culture/politics in the RDX contrast pairs; F19 is the laboratory narrative, F20 the clinical one). Ten meaning units: Bastian examines a biopsy / the biopsy shows amyloid deposits / the deposits consist of misfolded amyloid in plaques / the laboratory finds a tau protein / Bastian requests a scan / the scan reveals more plaques / the patient's daughter asks questions / Bastian explains the misfolding with a drawing / the team discusses the treatment options / Bastian gives the family the treatment plan. Domain vocabulary in both languages: amyloid/Amyloid, deposits/Ablagerungen, plaques/Plaques, misfolded/fehlgefaltet, Fehlfaltung, tau protein/Tauprotein. Subjects alternate between the protagonist (Bastian), a relative (the patient's daughter), institutions (the laboratory, the team) and objects (the biopsy, the deposits, the scan), singular and plural, so C3 switches cross real subject-verb agreement. No separable German verbs ('nachweisen', 'anordnen', 'aufzeigen', 'durchsprechen' avoided: 'findet', 'veranlasst', 'enthüllt', 'bespricht'; 'untersucht', 'bestehen aus', 'erklärt' are inseparable). Present tense and positive polarity; unit 9 reads naturally in German, units 1 and 10 in English, unit 10 is the closing sentence. Unit 8 says 'the protein's misfolding' / 'die Fehlfaltung des Proteins' rather than 'the misfolded protein' / 'das fehlgefaltete Protein': a segment-final bare 'Protein' is the one German word in this domain that lsne.lang_id labels 'E' (it is in the English lexicon and capitalised mid-sentence), and the genitive phrase keeps the segment unambiguously German without touching lsne/lang_id.py. For the same reason the tau protein is written as the closed compound 'Tauprotein': the token-level word grouping breaks 'Tau-Protein' at the hyphen and would label the stray 'Protein' English, which inflates the measured switch count inside a German stretch. 'Bastian' is the only proper name and is not in the lexicon's name list; being cue-less and capitalised it is labelled 'N' and excluded from the accuracy counts, so no lexicon edit was needed.
